purpose: 09 §6 item 5: a dated list of the challenge literature's topics, typed by the 09 §1 typology, to turn the §3 observation that 'the public challenge concentrates on D and X' into a count.

types.R: radiative mechanism (whether the greenhouse effect exists and its first-order size)
types.D: data (provenance, adjustment, homogenization, trends in observed series, including software that produces them)
types.X: proxy inference (reconstructions, tree rings, 'hide the decline')
types.M: method (physical models against observations; which instrument licenses the inference)
types.A: attribution (how much of observed change is human; natural causes)
types.Q: magnitude within a shared framework (sensitivity, feedbacks, forcing)
types.PROC: procedure: IPCC drafting and review, peer review and journals, freedom of information and data access, the conduct of inquiries
types.SOC: sociological: funding, incentives, institutional capture, denigration or suppression of dissent
types.POL: policy, economics, impacts outside the physical science

statements_method: Topics are the distinct claims each statement makes as recorded in 08 §4–5 from the statements read in the original; each distinct claim is one count, typed by what kind of evidence would settle it (09 §1). 'conceded' marks what the statement grants to the mainstream; 'contested' what it asserts against it. Only contested topics enter the tallies.

commons_2010.source: House of Commons Science and Technology Committee, HC 387 (2009–10), written evidence, memoranda CRU 01–57 as published at publications.parliament.uk/pa/cm200910/cmselect/cmsctech/387b/387we02.htm … 387we56.htm (55 memoranda, including three supplementary), plus the Global Warming Policy Foundation's CRU 27 from the printed volume HC 387-II. Not reached at those addresses: CRU 48, 49, 53 and 54 (institutional submissions — the list of written evidence names the Met Office, the University of East Anglia, the Government Chief Scientific Adviser, the Climate Change E-mails Review team and Richard Thomas among submitters not found).
commons_2010.method: Each memorandum was read by an automated summarizer (WebFetch, 2026-10-03) under a fixed instruction to list every distinct topic or allegation in one line and tag it DATA / PROXY / FOI / PEER / IPCC / MODEL / SENS / ATTR / SOLAR / INQ / OTHER, and to state the submitter's stance. The lines were recorded as given (577 + 8). The tags were mapped to the typology's types (DATA→D, PROXY→X, FOI/PEER/IPCC/INQ→PROC, MODEL→M, SENS→Q, ATTR and SOLAR→A) and the 103 OTHER lines sorted by keyword into SOC, D, PROC, POL, R, FRAME and NOISE, with the result inspected line by line. Five memoranda (McKitrick CRU 31, McIntyre CRU 32, Montford CRU 36, Peiser CRU 38, Institute of Physics CRU 39) were compared with the memoranda as known to the project and found faithfully summarized; the memoranda were not otherwise read in full. A topic line is one count; memoranda differ in length (3 to 95 paragraphs), so the memorandum-level counts (how many memoranda raise a type at all) are the safer measure.
